outcome: A slice contract can declare a check that requires containment, and the engine executes it at the host boundary, journals its exit code and bounded output, and binds the result as evidence a verifier reads rather than re-runs - with provenance explicit enough that host-executed evidence can never be mistaken for in-worker evidence.

exclude: executing anything not declared in an approved contract
changing what the existing checks assert

acceptance.text: A contract check marked as requiring containment is executed by the engine on the host at a defined boundary; its exit code and bounded output are journaled as a durable effect bound to the exact slice, candidate and contract digest.

Recorded check evidence carries explicit provenance naming the host boundary, and a verifier reading it can distinguish host-executed evidence from evidence a role produced itself; unlabelled or absent provenance fails closed.
The runner executes only checks declared in the approved contract for the slice under delivery. An input that is not such a declared check is refused, and the refusal is journaled.

Check output is bounded with truthful truncation markers and the run is bounded by a timeout; a check that times out or overflows is recorded as a failure with its diagnostic, never as a pass or as absent.

The verifier role instructions tell a verifier to read the engine's recorded host-boundary evidence for a declared containment-requiring check instead of re-running it, and every digest pinning those role assets is updated in the same candidate so no declared required check regresses.

constraints: The host runner is privileged surface: it may execute only checks declared in an approved contract, never arbitrary or model-supplied input.
Host-executed evidence is labelled as such at the point of recording, not inferred downstream.
Worker containment is unchanged; no production binary gains an uncontained dispatch path.
The e2e check in this slice's own list is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository; the candidate diff carries only product changes.
Changing a role asset changes its identity: every pin of that identity, wherever it is asserted, is part of this deliverable.
